crime: In her first week at the prison, the girl saved a place setting for {WITCH_NAME} in the dining hall so they could eat together. Today, in their cell, {WITCH_NAME} kept redrawing the fringe of the girl's scarf until every strand was even. As soon as she finished, the girl piled a bundle of mending before her and said they would not share supper unless she completed it all.

{WITCH_NAME} strangled the girl to death with the scarf. Then she flattened the scarf into a drawing, redrew it as a smooth, closed loop, and restored it. The scarf returned as a smooth noose enclosing the girl's neck and suspending her from the upper bunk. One prisoner believed the girl had hanged herself.

But when the prisoner examined the apparent slipknot, she found no knot to undo: the crossing was one seamless join. The fixed loop was also too narrow to have passed over the girl's head. Together, those impossibilities revealed that {WITCH_NAME} had used her Magic to stage the apparent hanging.
fields.epitaph: Her seat beside a friend should never have been something she had to earn.
execution: The execution stand clamps the witch to a gridded drawing board, with her head beyond its margin. A paper trimmer runs along that margin and severs her neck. Her cropped body remains motionless within the grid.

magic.name: Drawn Anew
magic.text: She can flatten inanimate objects into editable drawings, then lift them back out transformed to match her edits.
